about: One named thread whose wall clock is split by state in four known phases: on the cpu, asleep, waiting for a lock another thread holds, and runnable behind a rival process pinned to its core. A known split of wall clock by state.

trust.on_cpu: exact to a few microseconds on the thread's cpu clock; the contended phase adds its own 0.30 s on the cpu, so the thread's on-cpu time is 0.90 s
trust.sleeping: at least what was asked, longer by the scheduler's slack
trust.futex: the holder sleeps 0.40 s under the lock; the worker waits that long less the moment between the holder taking it and the worker asking, a few hundred microseconds
trust.runqueue: the worker and a rival process are pinned to one core and burn 0.30 s of cpu each; the worker waits on the run queue while the rival runs, about 0.30 s, more on a busy machine (other tasks on that core), less when the rival starts late. Only a lower bound of half of it is held
trust.tail_s: after its last phase the program idles `tail_s`, so that a poll of its on-cpu time every 250 ms has a point after the last of its cpu: a poll that would come after the exit cannot read a process that is gone
